title: Pluggable appenders and config
idea: An extensible logger lets you add outputs, layouts and filters as new classes registered by name, then wire them from configuration without editing Logger.
points: A new layout is a new `Formatter` class: the strategy pattern.
A filter wraps any appender in another `Appender`: the decorator pattern.
A builder assembles a Logger step by step, from code or from config.
A registry maps config names to factories; unknown names fail at startup.

hero.caption: Everything that varies is a plug-in. The level scale is the one closed set; change it rarely.

code.title: Strategy, decorator, builder
code.caption: A config file picks the outputs; a JSON formatter and an alerts output are added without touching Logger.

walk.text: Formatters by name. JsonFormatter is a plug-in, not an edit.
Appender factories by name. Each builds an appender around a formatter.
Config: INFO overall; the alerts output gets JSON and ERROR only.
Build from config, then log three levels.
An unknown output name is refused while building, not on the first log call.
The decorator passes a record on only at or above its own level.
`fromConfig` looks up each name, rejects an unknown output or format, and wraps it when `minLevel` is set.

pitfalls: Do not add `kafka` if-branches inside `Logger`; register a factory instead.
Validate configuration when the logger is built, not when the first line arrives.
In JSON output escape quotes, backslashes and control characters like newlines, or a message forges lines.

quiz.q: How many lines does Extensions print that start with `alerts`?
quiz.why: DEBUG is cut by the Logger threshold. INFO reaches the decorator but is below ERROR. Only the ERROR record passes, formatted as JSON.

takeaway: Add classes and register them; Logger itself never changes.
